BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r3.claim: Kāshifī says “their brother” means compassionate kinship, since Lot was an outsider, not their blood relative.
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r3.anchor: وذلك لأن لوطا ليس من نسبهم وكان أجنبيا منهم

BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r4.claim: Lot migrated with his paternal uncle Abraham to Syria; Abraham settled him in Jordan, where God sent him to Sodom; Lot was Hārān’s son, and Hārān was Tarikh’s brother.
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r4.anchor: فأنزله إبراهيم الأردن فأرسله الله إلى أهل سدوم

BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r5.claim: Lot urges them to fear God’s punishment for idolatry and sins.
BURSEVI:v6p218#3/r5.anchor: {ألا تتقون} ألا تخافون من عقاب الله تعالى على الشرك والمعاصي.

STUDYQURAN:26:160/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:160/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:160/r1.claim: Lot’s story opens like other prophetic accounts, including the earlier and later messenger narratives cited here.
STUDYQURAN:26:160/r1.anchor: For a similar opening to other prophets’ stories, cf. vv. 105–9, 123–27, 141–45, 176–80.

TAB-FULL:v17p629/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p629/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p629/r1.claim: Lot’s people denied the messengers when their brother Lot called them to fear God.

TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.claim: Al-Tabatabai says Lot's preceding argument rests on a demonstrative proof to which the discussion points, also reflected in the parallel wording cited from al-ʿAnkabut.
TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.anchor: وقد ظهر من جميع ما مر أن كلامه عليه السلام مبني على حجة برهانية أشير إليها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r2.claim: Lot is their brother by lineage, not by religion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r2.anchor: {إذ قال لهم أخوهم لوط} [الشعراء: 161] أخوهم في النسب، وليس بأخيهم في الدين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r3.claim: Lot calls them to fear God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r3.anchor: {ألا تتقون} [الشعراء: 106] ، يعني: ألا تخشون الله، يأمرهم أن يتقوا الله.

ELMALILI:26:160-175/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r1.claim: Lūṭ asks his people whether they will not fear God.
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r1.anchor: O vakit ki kardeşleri Lût onlara demişti: “Siz Allah’tan korkmaz mısınız? (161).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:160/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:160/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:160/r1.claim: Lot was Haran’s son and Abraham’s nephew; he left Iraq for Palestine with Abraham, then was sent to reform the unbelieving people of Sodom and Gomorrah, whose practices included homosexuality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:160/r1.anchor: Lût aleyhisselâm, Hz. İbrâhim’in kardeşi Haran’ın oğludur. İbrâhim aleyhisselâm ile birlikte Irak’tan ayrılıp Filistin’e gitmiş

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.claim: Samarrāʾī distinguishes Midian from the Aykah people: Shuaib belonged to Midian, so he is called their brother when addressing Midian but not Aykah; the other Shuʿara prophets address their own peoples.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.anchor: ومدين غير أصحاب الأيكة، وشعيب عليه السلام كان من مدين ولم يكن من أصحاب الأيكة ولذلك إذا ذكرت مدين قال: (أخوهم)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p440/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p440/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p440/r1.claim: The opening messenger appeal and command to fear God and obey Lot recur in earlier anecdotes and were explained there.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p440/r1.anchor: These verses occur in the previous anecdotes also. They have been explained there.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r17.claim: Lot was their brother by residence, not lineage: he was Abraham's nephew from Babylon.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r17.anchor: أي في السكنى في البلد لا في النسب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r18.claim: His long residence, marriage into their community, children with their women, and shared rural life explain the description as brother.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r19.claim: The appeal asks whether they fear God enough to protect themselves from His displeasure.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p382/r19.anchor: أي تخافون الله فتجعلوا بينكم وبين سخطه وقاية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r1.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r1.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says the codices of Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy, and Ḥafṣa read إذ قال لهم لوط, omitting أخوهم.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r1.anchor: قال النقاش إن في مصحف ابن مسعود وأبي وحفصة «إذ قال لهم لوط» وسقط «أخوهم»

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.claim: Lūṭ was Lūṭ son of Hārān son of Āzar, Abraham's nephew.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.anchor: لوط بن هاران بن آزر، وهو ابن أخي إبراهيم الخليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.claim: God sent Lūṭ to a great people during Abraham's lifetime; they lived in Sodom and its environs, later made into a foul lake in al-Ghawr near Jerusalem and between al-Karak and al-Shawbak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.anchor: في حياة إبراهيم، وكانوا يسكنون "سدوم" وأعمالها التي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.claim: Lūṭ called his people to worship God alone, obey the messenger sent to them, and avoid disobeying God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.anchor: فدعاهم إلى الله، عز وجل، أن يعبدوه وحده لا شريك له، وأن يطيعوا رسولهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.claim: Lūṭ forbade their unprecedented sexual transgression: approaching males instead of the women God created for them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.anchor: ونهاهم عن معصية الله، وارتكاب ما كانوا قد ابتدعوه في العالم، مما لم يسبقهم الخلائق إلى فعله

JISHUMI:v7p5380/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r4.claim: Lūṭ may be a foreign name or derive from sticking; the report about Abu Bakr calls a child more attached to the heart, and anything adhering to something has lāṭ to it.
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r4.anchor: (لوط) قيل: اسم أعجمي، ويحتمل أنه من اللوط وهو اللصوق، ومنه حديث أبي بكر

MUQATIL:26:160-173/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r2.claim: Lot was Lūṭ ibn Ḥarāz ibn Āzar, and Sarah was Lot’s sister.
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r2.anchor: ولوط بن حراز بن آزر، فسارة أخت لوط، عليه السلام

MUQATIL:26:160-173/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r3.claim: “Will you not be God-conscious?” means “Will you not fear God?”
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r3.anchor: يعنى ألا تخشون الله عز وجل
